dek: Three Katmai waterfalls with no entrance fee. Brooks Falls is the famous one; learn which parts of Brooks River need a permit from June 15 through October 31.
overview: Katmai National Park was established in 1918 around Novarupta and the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes. Today the park is also known for its salmon habitat and brown bears.

We cover three waterfalls. Brooks Falls, at the outlet of Lake Brooks, is the one visitors review. Fultons Falls and Wolverine Falls are also inside the park, but they have no reviews or trail lengths in our files, so there is little we can say about getting to them.
fallsIntro: Brooks Falls is the only one of the three with visitor reviews. Fultons Falls and Wolverine Falls are place names from the federal gazetteer, with no trail details.
plan: We don't have trail lengths for any of these waterfalls, so there is no hike to map out. The planning that matters here is the Brooks River permit rule in the fees section below. Brooks Falls is filed under Dillingham, about 101 miles away in a straight line, and the other two under Kodiak Station, so none of them is a day trip from a town.
feesLead: Entrance is free. A permit is needed only for activities in the Brooks River corridor from June 15 through October 31, and it is not needed on the viewing platforms.
access: The park says no permit is required for ordinary recreation outside the Brooks corridor rule. Getting to Brooks Camp is a trip of its own and our files don't include a road distance, so ask the park how to reach it.
safety: The Brooks River permit exists because of salmon season on that stretch of river, and the park is known for its brown bears. The park keeps the permit off the built boardwalks and viewing platforms so you can watch from the walkway. Read the park's permit pages before you go; we haven't covered distance or food-storage rules here.
